title: Worth doing soon: a reminders token another device writes after this device's erase read is dropped by the merge and its row stays live (a live row for an erased person)
evidence: Found in the S59b design (residual W3). Device A's erase reads the stored record once (packages/health-core/src/record-session-erase.ts ~:78, the s.sync.load() before the teardown, cancelRemindersForErase in widget-src/standalone/reminders.ts). Device B turns reminders on after that read: its new row and token land in the cloud file, and A never merges them in before its swap, so S59b's hr:remote-changed watcher never sees the token. A's flush then conflict-merges with B's file; the higher erase epoch wins and the opt-in is dropped (packages/health-core/src/merge.ts ~:787-830). The token is never in A's memory, so no cancel is sent: B's server row stays live and keeps emailing a person whose record is erased, until its email unsubscribe link is used. A second route, found in S59b's review (the adversary and Codex R1) and pinned as it stands in widget-src/standalone/reminders-erase-cancel.test.ts ('Limit (H126): a token a running save folds in ...'): a save already running at Delete folds B's token into A's working copy during the prepare's proof wait, but RecordSession.saveLoop announces hr:remote-changed once, when its last pass lands (packages/health-core/src/record-session.ts ~:442-446), which is after the swap; the working copy then holds the erased opt-in, so S59b's watcher reads no token and the row stays live. A fix there needs the announce per adoption, or the erase to hand the tokens it drops to the teardown (engine). Owner lean for the design of the first route: a B-side re-check after its opt-in write lands (B re-reads; if the record moved to a newer erase that holds no active opt-in for its token, B cancels its own row), since it needs no merge change. US-11 AC4c (the Limit names this lead).
